subsystems.name: Regolith feedstock system
subsystems.role: Excavates, crushes and delivers local soil to the construction site.

subsystems.name: Sintering energy delivery
subsystems.role: Fuses regolith grains into solid layers using concentrated heat.

subsystems.name: Multi-layer shell
subsystems.role: Provides structure, thermal insulation and pressure containment.

subsystems.name: Vacuum sealing and maintenance
subsystems.role: Keeps the insulating gap at low pressure for years.

subsystems.name: Automated construction control
subsystems.role: Coordinates robots, sintering and layer geometry without humans.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal management
subsystems.role: Powers sintering and keeps the habitat at livable temperatures.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the site
buildSteps.detail: Level and compact the ground, removing large rocks to create a stable foundation pad.

buildSteps.title: Excavate regolith
buildSteps.detail: Robotic excavators dig up local soil and transport it to a processing station.

buildSteps.title: Process feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Crush and sieve the regolith to a uniform grain size, discarding oversized fragments.

buildSteps.title: Deposit first layer
buildSteps.detail: Spread a thin, even layer of regolith and sinter it with a laser or microwave beam to form a solid base.

buildSteps.title: Build layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: Repeat deposition and sintering to raise the outer shell, moving the beam or deposition head over each new layer.

buildSteps.title: Create the vacuum gap
buildSteps.detail: Leave a gap between the outer shell and an inner shell, with periodic support pillars sintered or placed to hold them apart.

buildSteps.title: Install inner liner
buildSteps.detail: Add a gas-tight layer — either a sealed sintered surface or a polymer membrane — to contain breathable air.

buildSteps.title: Seal and evacuate
buildSteps.detail: Seal the gap edges, connect a vacuum pump, and evacuate the gap to reduce heat loss.

buildSteps.title: Outfit and test
buildSteps.detail: Install airlock, life support and power; pressurise the habitat and test for leaks and thermal performance.

prerequisites.why: Demonstrated in laboratory vacuum chambers, but not yet at habitat scale or with actual lunar or Martian soil.

prerequisites.tech: High-power, space-qualified lasers or microwave sources
prerequisites.why: Industrial versions exist; space versions must survive launch, vacuum, dust and wide temperature swings.
Robots can build simple structures on Earth, but full autonomy for off-world construction is unproven.
Keeping a multi-metre shell at vacuum for years without leaks is beyond current engineering practice.
Regolith handling has been tested in labs and small demonstrations, but not at production scale.

pathway.milestone: Laboratory sintering of regolith simulants in vacuum and thermal cycling tests
pathway.unlocks: understanding of material properties and energy needs.

pathway.milestone: Robotic construction of small test shells on the Moon or Mars
pathway.unlocks: validation of automation, dust tolerance and sintering in real conditions.

pathway.milestone: Full-scale habitat shell with vacuum insulation tested on the lunar surface
pathway.unlocks: proof that the design can hold pressure and temperature.

pathway.milestone: Crewed habitats and then settlements built from local material
